summary: The verifier runs the documented command on 29 sealed held-out evidence sets (15 families, one per rule/boundary) and compares the complete seven-key report: exact typed values, the three list fields as duplicate-free string sets, and initial_access key-by-key. Spot-traces of the readable clock (H066393), rootlogin (H30dd19) and case-1 evidence against the sealed expectations match the guide. They include the inclusive 600 s hostile window, a 691 s near-miss decoy, both clock-step signs, a shared-password legitimate login, package-write exclusion, an mtime/ctime decoy and an open session. No false rejection of contract-valid output and no plausible wrong implementation that passes was found.

case-1 minor files not opened (home/tpham/.ssh/authorized_keys, root/.ssh/authorized_keys, var/lib/dpkg/info/*.list); they are not needed for any verifier-soundness conclusion

checks_performed: Traced test.sh -> pytest -> _seal_app/_load/_run_case/_differences end to end, including the reward write only on pytest rc 0

Checked that _differences requires exactly the seven report.md keys, type-strict equality for times and null, and duplicate-free string sets for sources/accounts/persistence (report.md:3-25 vs test_outputs.py:114-128)

Checked that the candidate invocation matches the instruction: same python:3.13-slim-bookworm digest in both Dockerfiles, stdlib only (the -I -S flags only drop site-packages), /app/docs recopied with identical hashes, and evidence read-only and neutrally named 'evidence' so no family or case label leaks

Hand-traced the clock case H066393 against its expected row: remote vs auth.log gives a -475 s step; 193.236.16.41 btmp failures 1836700419..1836701019 are exactly 600 s, the inclusive boundary; decoy ivan@45.61.237.153 is 5 failures over 691 s and then a success, so not hostile; persistence ctimes 1836701639-1836702090 fall inside the first backup session; last_activity is the sudo at 16:57:32Z

Hand-traced the rootlogin case H30dd19: the -359 s step reproduces the expected first_activity 23:31:42Z from btmp; the root password login from the hostile address gives privilege_escalation = last_activity = 02:20:02Z with the session open; legitimate jenkins logins from 10.84.149.43 are correctly excluded from sources; the /etc/cron.d/debsums package write (0 s) is excluded; the /etc/cron.d/certbot-renew mtime lies inside the intruder session but its ctime (true 01:05:47Z) lies between intruder sessions and is excluded

Traced case-1 partially: the git authorized_keys, rc.local and apt-cache-clean ctimes match the timestamped root history and fall inside the first intruder session after the +6036 s correction; apt-listchanges is a package write inside the session and is excluded; certbot-renew (true 17:26:36Z) lies in a gap between intruder sessions and is excluded; the concurrent legitimate git login from 10.233.9.93 is excluded from sources

Checked family facts for sign and range partitions: step_sign +1 and -1 both present, step_s 30 and 7200, offsets -720/+840 and quarter hours 330/345/525/570/-210, year rollovers, auth_files 1..6, escalated true/false, open_session true/false
Checked that the exact comparison is not a representation false rejection: list order is free, and the time format and key set are fixed by report.md
Checked the verifier's time budget (DEADLINE 1650 s, per case min(300, remaining), floor 30 s) against 29 small cases

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if it is missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Every rule has a named family, and each family compares the full report, so a missing rule changes at least one compared field: rule 1 clock/year/tz, rule 2 brute/rotation, rule 4 key, rule 5 sudo/rootlogin, rule 6 ctime, rule 7 open, plus edge and broad families.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result, not existence, keys or row count
coverage_sweep.reason: _differences compares every value of all seven keys exactly; sets are compared by sorted equality with a duplicate check.

coverage_sweep.category: Isolating case per named domain rule
coverage_sweep.reason: The readable traces confirm isolating cases for the inclusive 600 s bound and its >600 s near miss (clock), both step signs (clock facts), the shared-password non-tie (rootlogin, case-1), root-login escalation without sudo (rootlogin), package-write exclusion (case-1, rootlogin), mtime vs ctime (rootlogin certbot-renew) and the open session not counted as an event (rootlogin, open). A dedicated test for the exactly-2-seconds package tolerance could not be confirmed from readable extractions, because the ctime family is sealed. This is breadth within rule 6, not a demonstrated wrong outcome.

Traced these wrong solutions against the readable cases; each changes a compared field. Constant or empty report: 29 distinct expectations. Strict <600 window: clock H066393 initial_access. Counting any 5 failures: ivan decoy becomes initial access. Host time without step correction: all time fields in the clock cases. mtime instead of ctime: rootlogin certbot-renew and touch -r on authorized_keys. All logins to the intruder account: extra source 10.84.149.43 or 10.233.9.93. collected_utc as last activity: rootlogin last_activity.

List order is free and JSON is parsed rather than byte-compared. The only fixed representations (seven keys, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, null for no escalation, initial_access sub-keys) are all stated in report.md. The isolated interpreter flags only affect non-stdlib imports, which the instruction forbids.

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions and lifecycle (unprivileged, read-only evidence, no network, stdlib, no dependence on /app/evidence)
coverage_sweep.reason: The run uses uid 65534 with no_new_privs and root-owned 0444/0555 evidence. _seal_app removes /app/evidence so dependence on it fails. Grading uses held-out hosts, so embedding case-1 answers cannot pass.

coverage_sweep.category: Stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, Oracle-specific representation, unreachable cases
coverage_sweep.reason: Expectations are sealed files pinned by ROSTER hashes, and the candidate cannot read /tests (probe test). The report is read from a fresh candidate-owned scratch directory on each case, and the evidence is regenerated from the tar on each case. Every case lies inside the instruction's variation domain (facts: offsets, years 2019-2031, 1-6 auth files, step 30-7200 s).

coverage_sweep.category: State machine initialization-to-first-event and signed derived quantities
coverage_sweep.reason: The clock-step sign is discriminated: clock and edge families contain both +1 and -1 steps and cases without a step. Session state from login to first logout, and a session open at collection, are both exercised (open_session true/false; rootlogin root session open).
Failures name the case id, the differing keys, the exit code and a stderr tail. Each test maps to one rule family.
